messages:
Alex P: Quick follow-up from the RFC — I sketched a 'soft-reserve' admission idea to reduce tenant starvation when queues get tight. Thoughts?
Maria G: curious, what do you mean by soft-reserve vs current lease tokens?
Alex P: current leases are all-or-nothing. soft-reserve = small, reclaimable headroom credit that lets tiny low-cost requests skip long waits but can be revoked quickly when a big batch needs capacity.
Jamal: sounds useful for short prompt fastpath, but worried about cache pin churn if we let too many through.
Sasha: yeah, KV cache pinning is the killer. tiny requests that create new kv entries then get evicted immediately -> eviction storm.
Maria G: can we scope soft-reserve only to requests that touch <= N cache keys or TTL < T?
Alex P: exactly. proposal: soft-reserve metadata includes "max_kv_keys" and "eviction_score_hint". The scheduler will reject soft-reserve admits if predicted eviction_score > threshold.
Jamal: how do we predict eviction_score cheaply? model complexity -> bad.
Alex P: use recent LRU-weighted metrics + request profiling. not perfect but better than blind admits.
Sasha: operationally we need clear interface between scheduler and batcher: scheduler says "admit soft-reserve token X" and batcher must be able to preempt it without expensive io.
Alex P: agreed. draft handshake proto: 
```
message AdmitRequest {
  string tenant_id = 1;
  bool soft_reserve = 2;
  uint32 max_kv_keys = 3;
  float eviction_hint = 4; // 0..1
}
message AdmitResponse {
  bool accepted = 1;
  string lease_id = 2;
  uint32 ttl_seconds = 3;
  enum Preemptability { NON_PREEMPTIBLE = 0; SOFT_PREEMPT = 1; }
  Preemptability p = 4;
}
```
Maria G: nice. I would add a field for expected token_cost_estimate so billing and cost heuristics can be considered.
Alex P: good call. Jamal, your call: should soft-reserve be global-per-GPU or per-lane?
Jamal: per-lane. Global soft-reserve will be gamed by tenants that send lots of tiny requests. Per-lane lets us respect isolation and batching efficiency.
Sasha: also need hysteresis on eviction. If we preempt soft-reserve, add cooldown so the same tenant doesn't immediately reapply and thrash queues.
Alex P: implement as backoff window and a soft-failure reason: "preempted:cooldown" in AdmitResponse.
Maria G: how do we surface metrics? ops need visibility into how many soft-reserves, preempts, kv-evictions triggered.
Alex P: add telemetry events: soft_reserve_granted, soft_reserve_preempted, soft_reserve_revoked_cooldown, soft_reserve_eviction_impact.
Jamal: don't forget SLO impacts — if we allow soft-reserve for latency-critical tenants, we could accidentally increase tail latencies if preemption happens during response assembly.
Sasha: mitigate by disallowing soft-reserve for requests with predicted long-running streams or high token counts. Keep it for requests < ~64 tokens and streaming=false.
Maria G: can we prototype with a feature flag? route 10% traffic to lane with soft-reserve enabled, collect evictions and tail latency.
Alex P: yes — rollout plan: feature-flagged per-cluster, telemetry + scorecard after 24h. If eviction delta < 1% and p50 latency improves, expand.
Jamal: small nit: name it "grace-credit" in code to avoid confusion with existing "reserve" semantics.
Sasha: ops playbook: if evictions spike, toggle to reject soft_reserve or lower max_kv_keys to 0 (stateless fastpath only).
Maria G: what about cost accounting? Some tenants could exploit soft-reserve to get latency but increase cost.
Alex P: include cost_estimate in admit response and emit per-tenant cost_hint. Billing can use it for post-hoc adjustments. Also we can gate on account tier.
infra-bot: deploy-checklist: add admit API v0.3 to canary cluster, add feature flag `enable_grace_credit`, add telemetry events and SLO dashboard panels.
Jamal: one last thought — we should avoid coupling the allocator to request semantics. Keep admit API small and let higher layers annotate heuristics.
Alex P: agreed. scheduler only enforces numeric constraints, no per-tenant policy language. policy lives in fleet-controller.
Sasha: sounds like a path forward. I'll draft an RFC update with the proto, cooldown/backoff semantics, and rollout plan.
Maria G: thanks — please include the telemetry queries we'll need for the 24h scorecard.
Alex P: will do. If nobody objects by EOD I'll start the canary patch tomorrow. :thumbsup:
